The purpose of this study was to explore the experiences of oncology nurses caring for adults with sickle disease (SCD), to identify the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of nurses, and to identify strategies to improve care of patients with SCD.
Sickle cell disease (SC) is a genetic disorder in which there is a mutation in the gene that produces hemoglobin, the protein responsible for carrying oxygen in the body.
Sickle cell disease (SCA) is a chronic disease that is associated with a high risk of mortality and morbidity, and the role of the oncology nurse is to provide care to these patients.
